connector.modeled: Owner decision 2026-11-05: no SMA/coax; 50 ohm vertical AddLumpedPort at the line start (board edge y=-13), strip width, R=50 ohm; S11 reference plane = line start, no de-embedding (run with --edge-port lumped). Feed: 50 ohm line (w 3.92 mm, y -13 -> -9.851) + lambda/4 transformer (w 0.80 mm, l 6.60 mm) touching the radiating edge y=-3.251 (no inset, no notch).

feed.line_width_method: Hammerstad-Jensen (with Wheeler 35 um thickness correction) on eps_r 4.4, h 2.07 mm: w = 3.919 mm -> 3.92 mm gives Z0 = 49.99 ohm, eps_eff = 3.308 (estimate, GEOMETRY_ONLY)
feed.transformer_width_method: Hammerstad-Jensen static Z0 (Wheeler 35 um correction): w 0.80 mm -> Zt 102.5 ohm; Kirschning-Jansen eps_eff(f0) 3.197 (GUIDE_MODEL)

parasitic_params.note: Floating sheet (no via, no probe), same metal as the patch. The polygon stays inside y>=-3.0 so no part of it lies under the 0.8 mm transformer / 50 ohm line (patch edge y=-3.251, transformer at y<-3.251 on z=h).

parasitic_patches: par1: 11.0 x 7.6 mm floating sheet at z=1.035 mm (x -5.5..5.5, y -3.0..4.6)
US3_MS3.note: Single change: ONE buried parasitic patch is added. Patch (11.421 x 6.502 mm), U-slot (Wu 4.4, Lu 2.65, t 0.8, y0 -0.7), feed (50 ohm line 3.92 mm + 0.80 x 6.60 mm transformer, port at y=-13), FR4 (eps_r 4.4, tan_delta 0.017, h 2.07 mm homogeneous), board 26 x 26 mm, metal and mesh hint are identical to US3_MS3. patch_L and the transformer are NOT retuned on purpose (the first EM run must show what the parasitic does by itself; retuning is a refinement round).

rationale: Owner request 2026-11-15: US3_MS3 in HFSS has -10 dB over 7.740-8.090 GHz (~350 MHz, worst -6.8 dB) and a single resonance; the HFSS patch_L sweep only shifts it (-7 MHz per +0.01 mm, width fixed ~350 MHz) and round 29 showed that widening the U only lowers the patch mode. A second coupled resonance is needed (coupled-resonator broadening), as in the EuCAP stacked element (driven patch on top, buried parasitic below). Choices: (1) z=h/2=1.035 mm (h1=h2): heuristic of maximum coupling between driven patch and parasitic for a capacitive divider (V_par/V_top = h1/(h1+h2), parasitic energy fraction ~ h1*h2/(h1+h2)^2 is maximal at h1=h2); too close to the ground (small h1) the parasitic has V~0 and decouples and has a high Q, too close to the patch (small h2) the two behave as one thicker patch. This is a heuristic, not verified; it also gives two equal dielectrics (1.035 mm) = 2 dielectrics + 3 copper layers. (2) Size 11.0 x 7.6 mm: the parasitic is embedded in eps_r 4.4 (eps_eff_p ~4.2-4.4, little fringing into air), so it must be LONGER than a top-air patch of the same frequency (unslotted P01_MS1 is 7.322 mm at 7.991 GHz in HFSS) and longer than the slot-loaded driven patch (6.502 mm); the guide gives Lp ~7.6 mm for f2 ~7.99 GHz (HFSS frame, f2/f1 ~1.01). (3) Offset +0.8 mm in y, not centred: a centred 7.6 mm sheet would overhang the radiating edge y=-3.251 by 0.55 mm and run under the 0.8 mm transformer (local Z0 change of a high-Z section, uncontrolled); with y_min=-3.0 the whole sheet is clear of the feed and the 1.349 mm overhang goes to +y (opposite to the feed side; expected, not verified, to counter the known -y tilt of 10-15 deg). (4) Width 11.0 mm (0.2 mm inset from the patch x edges) to avoid loading the non-radiating edges. (5) patch_L and the transformer unchanged: one variable only, so that the splitting/shift can be read from the EM run. GEOMETRY_ONLY; no S11, gain, efficiency or bandwidth is claimed.

computation.label: GUIDE_MODEL (geometric estimate, NOT EM, no result)
computation.method: (a) Parasitic resonance: Hammerstad/Jensen patch formula (eps_eff and DeltaL) with h=h1=1.035 mm, W=11.0 mm and eps_eff_p in 4.0-4.4 (embedded, ~eps_r), multiplied by the ratio 0.931 = f_HFSS(P01_MS1)/f_formula(P01_MS1) (7.991/8.580 GHz) to take out the systematic offset of the formula for this FR4 stack (assumes the same offset applies to the embedded patch; unverified). (b) Coupled response: two-resonator coupled-mode model (S11 = 1 - (2/Qe)*[A^-1]_11, A=[[1/Qe+1/Qu1+2j(f-f1)/f0, jk],[jk, 1/Qu2+2j(f-f2)/f0]]), Qe=Qu1=15 chosen so the single-resonator baseline reproduces the HFSS -10 dB width of US3_MS3 (model 7.738-8.092 GHz vs HFSS 7.740-8.090 GHz; the model does NOT reproduce the HFSS depth: worst in channel -5.7 dB vs HFSS -6.8 dB). Parasitic Qu2 25-35 assumed (dielectric Q=1/tan_delta=58.8 plus radiation of a half-height aperture; assumed, not computed). k is an unknown of the model: it is scanned, NOT derived from the geometry. Feed matching, transformer, U-slot and radiation resistance changes are not modelled.

outputs.uncertainty_f2: about +-4 % (+-0.3 GHz): eps_eff_p, the h1-only fringing and the calibration are all assumptions; the first EM run measures f2

coupled_model_two_resonances.needed_for_minus10_over_channel: k ~0.04-0.05 with f2/f1 = 1.00-1.02: model -10 dB band ~7.65-8.20 GHz (~530-580 MHz) and worst-in-channel -7.7 to -9.3 dB (model, Lorentzian single-mode shapes; it does not reproduce the HFSS depth of US3_MS3, so treat as order of magnitude of the widening, ~1.5x, not as a prediction)
coupled_model_two_resonances.k_0p02: band ~7.72-8.12 GHz (~400 MHz), worst in channel ~-6.3 dB
coupled_model_two_resonances.k_0p06: two humps with a dip above -10 dB between them (over-coupled), worst in channel ~-6 dB
coupled_model_two_resonances.split_at_f2_eq_f1: two modes split by ~k*f0 = 0.3-0.4 GHz for k 0.04-0.05
coupled_model_two_resonances.centering: in the model with f2/f1=1.01, k=0.04 the band centre is 7.93 GHz (lower edge margin ~75 MHz, upper edge ~40 MHz short of 8.2368): a small patch_L reduction (~-0.05 mm, ~+35 MHz from the -7 MHz/0.01 mm HFSS sweep) would be the first retune, as a refinement, not in this variant

outputs.openEMS_vs_HFSS_frame: all frequencies above are in the HFSS frame (HFSS resonances ~0.9 % below openEMS); openEMS should show the same pattern ~+0.9 % higher

overlap.note: parasitic 11.0 x 7.6 mm; patch 11.421 x 6.502 mm

pre_registered_hypothesis.H1: In the same solver and mesh as US3_MS3 (openEMS 023 base: -10 dB 7.80-8.18 GHz, ~380 MHz, worst in channel -8.18 dB), US3_PS1 shows a second resonance feature (second local minimum of S11 or maximum of Re(Zin), or a loop in the Smith chart) between 7.5 and 8.6 GHz AND a contiguous -10 dB band >= 450 MHz; worst |S11| in 7.7376-8.2368 GHz <= -8.5 dB.
pre_registered_hypothesis.H2: Radiation pattern at f0 stays usable: Dmax within 20 deg of broadside (US3_MS3: 15 deg) and radiation efficiency >= 0.55 (US3_MS3: 0.65-0.67), beam squint over the channel in the E plane not worse than US3_MS3 (5.7 deg HFSS).
pre_registered_hypothesis.H3_null: If no second feature appears (single resonance, band ~350-400 MHz), the coupling is too weak or f2 is out of the 7.5-8.6 GHz window: the parasitic mode must be found first (Re(Zin)/field monitor) before changing anything.
pre_registered_hypothesis.decision_rule: Next round (one change only, max 2 refinements per candidate): (a) H1 holds and the band is just offset (one edge misses by <60 MHz): retune patch_L (guide -7 MHz per +0.01 mm; calibrate with the new run, the parasitic changes the slope). (b) A second feature is visible but off position or two humps with a dip above -10 dB in the band centre: change Lp (guide -9.6 MHz per +0.01 mm, i.e. +-0.1 mm = -+96 MHz, calibrate with the run) to move f2 closer (dip: bring f2 nearer to f1; band edge: move f2 toward the missing edge). (c) Single resonance only (no splitting although a second mode exists in the window) or splitting clearly too large (dip above -10 dB with f2 already close to f1): change z_par, the coupling lever (1.035 -> 0.80 or 1.30 mm, total h kept). The heuristic puts the maximum coupling at h1=h2, so moving z away from the middle should REDUCE k (use for the over-coupled/dip case); if the run shows too little splitting at h1=h2, the heuristic is wrong and the opposite direction must be tested from the run data, or Wp enlarged. Do not alter z and Lp in the same round. (d) H2 fails (Dmax > 20 deg or eta < 0.55) while S11 improves: reduce the +y overhang (shift the parasitic y_min/y_max toward the patch) before touching the feed. H1 and H2 both hold: fine mesh (two-mesh convergence rule), then owner decision on HFSS.
pre_registered_hypothesis.evidence_rule: Nothing here is a result. A single FDTD base-mesh run of US3_PS1 only tests the pre-registered hypotheses; HFSS is needed to validate.

manufacturability.layers: 3 copper layers (L1 patch + feed + U-slot at z=h, L2 floating parasitic at z=1.035 mm, L3 ground at z=0) and 2 dielectric layers of ~1.035 mm each: a standard 3-copper-layer FR4 multilayer (core + prepreg/core).
manufacturability.vias: none: the parasitic is floating (no probe, no plated through hole in the antenna region); the feed is a planar microstrip.
manufacturability.min_feature_mm: U-slot arms 0.8 mm and gaps as in US3_MS3 (unchanged); parasitic is a solid rectangle 11.0 x 7.6 mm, no feature < 0.8 mm.
manufacturability.stackup_note: Dielectric thickness and the exact z of the buried copper depend on the fabricator's core/prepreg library; typical core thicknesses of ~1.0-1.2 mm and prepreg of 0.1-0.2 mm are only an orientation (NOT verified against a datasheet). The model assumes ONE homogeneous eps_r=4.4 over 2.07 mm, so the fabricator must give the real stackup (the prepreg/core eps_r can differ from the core and sets z_par and k).
manufacturability.tolerances_to_specify: layer-to-layer registration and dielectric thickness ( +-z_par moves k and f2 ); etching of Lp (guide: ~10 MHz per 0.01 mm). Same rough FR4 + copper-roughness caveat as the rest of the campaign.
manufacturability.risks: z_par and registration are not controlled by the TFG; the model is homogeneous FR4 (provisional); a floating inner sheet cannot be seen or tuned after lamination.

purpose: Widen the US3_MS3 band with a second coupled resonance (buried parasitic) to cover 7.7376-8.2368 GHz with -10 dB margin, keeping a broadside pattern; first EM test of the parasitic format.
mesh_hint_note: Hard y line at -0.215 mm (inside the U-slot base, metal-free): microstrip_edge_qw adds plain y lines across the slot (<= 0.3 mm), which without this hint gave a y grading ratio 1.507 > 1.5 near y -0.37..-0.07 mm. Found by prepare-only trials (round 23). Same hint reused; parasitic z=1.035 mm and the x/y edge lines of the sheet are added by the solver (round 24 parasitic support), not by this file.
